key_insight: A quantics tensor-train (QTT) Chebyshev–Galerkin method solves global spectral boundary-value problems directly in compressed form while preserving their variational structure.
engineering_relevance: The method enables accurate linear-elasticity analysis across large design and uncertainty spaces without explicitly storing full solution arrays.
method: Assemble weak-form spectral systems directly as QTT representations.
Handle variable coefficients, mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet–Robin conditions.
Treat parameters and random inputs as extra coordinates for a single joint solve.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports errors below 10⁻⁸ on a 3D elasticity benchmark, 1.7×10⁷ cantilever designs solved in 92 s, and 2.4×10⁶-fold memory reduction versus a full coefficient array for a ten-random-coordinate problem.
watch_item: Computational savings depend on tensor compressibility; the reported benchmarks do not establish comparable gains for poorly compressible problems.
paper_title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev--Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
